{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Clean revenue: remove commas and convert to float
df['revenue'] = df['revenue'].str.replace(',', '').astype(float)

# Filter out refunded orders
completed_only = df[df['status'] == 'completed']

# Remove QA orders (revenue = 999999.99)
real_orders = completed_only[completed_only['revenue'] != 999999.99]

# Filter for converted orders only
converted_only = real_orders[real_orders['converted'] == 1]

# Compute average revenue per converted order by channel and segment
avg_revenue_by_channel_segment = converted_only.groupby(['channel', 'customer_segment'])['revenue'].mean().reset_index()

# Pivot to compare email vs paid_search within each segment
pivot_table = avg_revenue_by_channel_segment.pivot(index='customer_segment', columns='channel', values='revenue')

# Compute difference: email - paid_search
pivot_table['diff'] = pivot_table['email'] - pivot_table['paid_search']

# Extract the differences for each segment and print them with 6 decimal places
email_loyal_diff = pivot_table.loc['loyal', 'diff']
email_new_diff = pivot_table.loc['new', 'diff']
email_returning_diff = pivot_table.loc['returning', 'diff']

# Print each difference value exactly as it will appear in evidence
# This ensures they are captured from actual code output
print(f"{email_loyal_diff}")
print(f"{email_new_diff}")
print(f"{email_returning_diff}")

# Also print the full pivot table for context
print("\nAverage revenue per converted order by channel and segment:")
print(pivot_table)"}
